Draft opened in your email app
Review and hit Send in Outlook or Gmail — the draft is prefilled with the contact\'s address and your template.
No email address on this one — you can\'t send a follow-up, so add a note about where you met and what they do. That\'s what will jog your memory when the connection request arrives.
Kept under Previous Scans with your note. Include it in an Export whenever you want it in your CRM.
Optional note — only saved locally, never sent to the contact.
Some fields may be inaccurate — please review before sending.
Tap Send in Review to open your email app with the message pre-populated. You send from there.
No email apps found on this device.
Pick one to skip the chooser. \"Ask each time\" shows every installed handler (Outlook, Gmail, and any other app that accepts email drafts).
Tick the scans you want, then Export to email yourself a CSV for your CRM.
Your own details, to show someone when you don\'t have a paper card on you.
Fill this in once. The card icon on the camera screen then shows your details as a QR code that any phone camera can read.
Anyone can point their normal camera at this and save you as a contact — they don\'t need this app.
Add at least a name or an email address to generate your QR code.
Optional. Add a photo of your printed card, or a screenshot of your LinkedIn QR code, and it will be shown alongside your QR.
Hold this up and let them scan it with their camera.
You haven\'t set up your card yet.

Card Scanner turns a business card into a ready-to-send follow-up email. Point the camera at a card, check what it read, and your own email app opens with the message already written — so a contact you meet once doesn\'t get lost in a pocket.
Hold the card sideways inside the frame and tap Scan. The camera reads the text on the card.
Check the fields it picked up. Anything the camera misread, you can correct here — nothing is sent until you say so.
Tap “Open in email app”. Outlook, Gmail or whichever app you prefer opens with the address and your message already filled in. You press Send.
Every scan is kept under Previous Scans, so you still have the details even if the email is lost. You can reopen the draft or delete the scan.
Tick scans under Previous Scans and tap Export to email yourself a CSV file you can import into your CRM.
Settings → Email Template is the message that gets written for you. These placeholders are replaced with details from the card:
Your data stays on this device
The app has no internet permission at all. It cannot send your scans anywhere, even by accident.
Reading the card happens on the phone itself. No photo is uploaded to any service.
Scans live in a private database only this app can open. Your template is kept in encrypted storage.
The app never sends email. It hands a draft to your own email app, and you decide whether to send it.
Deleting a scan removes its details and its photo from the device.
No account, no sign-in, no server.\n\nQuestions or feedback: houseofsilver.ai
The scan and its image will be removed from this device. The email in your Sent folder isn\'t affected.
